title: Population and sample

blocks.heading: Population and sample
blocks.text: The research population is the whole defined group; a sample is the selected subset studied. The sampling method is the selection procedure, not the group itself. Findings need limits where the frame misses groups or responses are incomplete.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Research population
blocks.text: The research population is the whole group of units or people that the enquiry is intended to investigate. Define it before sampling: all households on the relevant settlement list differs from everyone in Namibia.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Research sample
blocks.text: The research sample is the selected subset of the research population from which data are collected. A list of 12 selected households describes a sample; choosing every fifth household describes the method.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: An invented study defines its population as households listed in two named settlements during a specified month. A sample selects some of those households for observation or voluntary questions. It cannot automatically represent households outside that area or later residents. A clear population definition makes it possible to assess what the sampling frame includes or misses.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
